failures.proposed_fix: Step 1 (diagnostic, no behaviour change): make helios-uitest print the elapsed seconds of every check and of each computeFlip call (image size and differing pixel count) and write them into report.json under --out; upload that file with the results artifact so a passing 472 s run is no longer opaque. Step 2 (fix, if the timings confirm ꟻLIP): keep the metric and its limits (mean <= 0.01, hot <= 0.1 %) but make render::computeFlip local: ꟻLIP's output is exactly 0 wherever the whole receptive field of both images is identical, so evaluate only the tiles (plus the kernel radius) that contain a differing pixel and add zeros elsewhere; mean/max/countAbove stay bit-identical. Add a doctest that the tiled result equals the full-image result on random pairs and a perf: case (2156x1438, a dozen differing pixels, Debug). Alternative or addition: compile flip.cpp with -O2 in the sanitizer presets (ASan stays on; optimisation level is not an ISA flag). Neither changes the 600 s TIMEOUT or skips the test.

Same job class, different outcome: 10-06 a1 (EPYC 7763) FAIL 19,696 pps 1.5222 % with background 0.78 / 0.84 and 0.75 / 0.31 and WARN '+25.8 % / +34.7 % outside the thread'; 10-06 a2 (same EPYC 7763 class) PASS 0.0000 % with background 0.16 / 0.16 and 0.22 / 0.12; 10-07 (Xeon 8573C) PASS 0.0000 % with background 0.09 / 0.19 and 0.12 / 0.16; owner's win-gpu fixed hardware PASS 0.0000 % on 10-06, 10-07 and 10-08. engine/net/README: a RIO socket buffers nothing beyond its posted receives (slots capped at 16,384, about 0.8 s at 20 kpps), so a receiver stall over about 0.8 s drops packets.

The binding NS-0.7 verdict stays the fixed-hardware win-gpu run.

- by-design: pcg_tests_perf in linux-gcc 'Perf gates' on both nights. avx2 was 2.95071 ms (ctest) and 2.97201 ms (doctest --perf) on 10-07, and 2.98128 ms and 2.99403 ms on 10-08, against 0.5 ms. This is K5b / ADR-0.9c. assetpipe_tests_perf passed both nights (4.02 s and 3.99 s), so its 10-06 failure did not recur.
- known-P0, deterministic: schemac_sql_postgres in linux-asan, 5 of 5 asan attempts since 10-06. The socket path is 108 bytes against a 107-byte limit; gcc (101) and clang (103) pass. Both nights also log the non-fatal UBSan report at tools/schemac/src/sema.cpp:757:32 (INT64_MAX + 1, the line is 'next = v.value + 1;'). The fixes are a short socket directory outside the build tree and an unsigned increment.
- new, and not what it looked like: editorui_ed15 in linux-asan. It is not random starvation, it is deterministic per host class. On the same commit it takes 26.51 s on a Xeon 8573C, about 473 s on an EPYC 9V74 (474.89 s on 10-06, 472.44 s on 10-08) and over 600 s on an EPYC 7763 (timeouts on 10-06 and 10-07). Other tests in the same jobs differ only 1.0-1.7x across those hosts. A re-run of this job is a lottery on the host class, and the EPYC 9V74 pass on 10-08 used 79 % of the 600 s TIMEOUT. My hypothesis is that the full ꟻLIP runs on four dark goldens (two at 2156x1438, 10-15 differing pixels each) in a Debug+ASan build on the AMD hosts. That is not proven. The first step is per-check timing in helios-uitest; the fix is a local or optimised computeFlip, with no threshold change.
- resource-starved:
  - windows-vs2026 NS-0.7 on 10-08: 19,777 pps, 1.1137 % drops. The NS-0.2 cross-checks just before it show background 0.41 / 0.84 and 1.37 cores on 4 CPUs.
